recommendations.text: In adults with aneurysmal SAH, do not routinely administer antifibrinolytic drugs before securing the ruptured aneurysm to improve functional outcome.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 1a; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: No evidence-based recommendation can be made for pressure-lowering drugs before treatment of the ruptured aneurysm to improve functional outcome in adult aSAH.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 1b; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Before aneurysm treatment, if systolic pressure remains >160–180 mmHg after analgesia, oral nimodipine and urinary catheter placement, consider antihypertensives targeting around 160 mmHg to reduce rebleeding risk.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 1b; consensus 1

recommendations.section: PICO 1b: How to lower pressure before repair
recommendations.text: If antihypertensives are used before aneurysm repair, favour a continuous infusion of a short-acting drug such as labetalol. Avoid diuretics to preserve normovolaemia. Lower pressure gradually and cautiously, with no more than a 10% MAP decrease during the first 2 hours, to limit delayed cerebral ischaemia risk.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 1b; consensus 2

recommendations.text: Evidence is insufficient to recommend treating the ruptured aneurysm as early as possible specifically to improve functional outcome in adult aSAH.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 2; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Aim to secure the ruptured aneurysm within 24 hours of ictus, coordinating timing so that the most dedicated expert team is available.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 2; consensus 1

recommendations.text: For adult aSAH in good clinical condition, WFNS I–III, with an anterior or posterior circulation aneurysm equally amenable to regular coiling without adjunctive devices or to clipping, prefer regular coiling to reduce poor functional outcome.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 3a; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Discuss every aSAH case in an interdisciplinary team that includes at least one neurosurgeon and one neurointerventionalist.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 3a; consensus 1

recommendations.section: PICO 3a: Choose the safest effective occlusion
recommendations.text: The team should choose the modality expected to provide the best outcome for the individual patient and the safest, optimal occlusion of that aneurysm.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 3a; consensus 2

recommendations.text: When selecting aneurysm treatment for patients younger than 45 years, consider the greater long-term protection of clipping compared with coiling.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 3a; consensus 3

recommendations.section: PICO 3a: Poor clinical condition at admission
recommendations.text: For aSAH admitted with GCS <13, use multidisciplinary assessment to choose treatment type and timing, accounting for the presumed cause of the poor clinical condition.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 3a; consensus 4

recommendations.text: For poor or worsening clinical condition caused by a space-occupying intracerebral or subdural haematoma, proceed to immediate surgery for clipping and haematoma removal.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 3a; consensus 5

recommendations.section: PICO 3b: Endovascular devices other than regular coils
recommendations.text: Evidence does not support a recommendation for alternative endovascular devices rather than regular coiling of a ruptured aneurysm to improve functional outcome.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 3b; recommendation 1

recommendations.section: PICO 3b: Aneurysms unsuitable for regular coiling
recommendations.text: If a ruptured aneurysm cannot be treated with regular coiling, a multidisciplinary team should weigh the safety, efficacy and durability of microsurgical and alternative endovascular options to select treatment.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 3b; consensus 1

recommendations.text: Reserve stent-assisted coiling for selected aSAH cases in which other treatment options are not feasible.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 3b; consensus 2

recommendations.text: Use flow diversion only as a last-line option for ruptured aneurysm treatment in aSAH.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 3b; consensus 3

recommendations.text: Give prophylactic oral nimodipine to adults with aSAH to reduce poor functional outcome.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 4; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Do not give tirilazad, statins, magnesium sulphate or endothelin-receptor antagonists prophylactically to improve functional outcome after aSAH.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 4; recommendation 2

recommendations.section: PICO 4: Antiplatelets or lumbar drainage as prophylaxis
recommendations.text: No recommendation can be made for prophylactic antiplatelets or lumbar drainage to improve functional outcome in aSAH pending further randomised evidence.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 4; recommendation 3

recommendations.text: For aSAH with clinical deterioration caused by delayed cerebral ischaemia, evidence does not establish a functional-outcome recommendation for induced hypertension.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 5a; recommendation 1

recommendations.section: PICO 5a: Selected use of induced hypertension
recommendations.text: Consider induced hypertension for clinical deterioration from DCI only after the aneurysm is secured and standard treatment has been insufficient. Weigh clinical contraindications and possible complications.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 5a; consensus 1

recommendations.text: No evidence-based recommendation can be made for endovascular vasospasm treatment to improve functional outcome in aSAH with deterioration from DCI.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 5b; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: For aSAH with DCI-related deterioration and refractory severe vasospasm, consider intra-arterial drug treatment as rescue therapy in selected patients.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 5b; consensus 1

recommendations.text: Routine balloon angioplasty is unsupported for DCI-related deterioration with refractory severe vasospasm. Selected cases may warrant it as last-line rescue after multidisciplinary discussion of risks and uncertain benefit.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 5b; consensus 2

recommendations.section: PICO 5b: Temporary retrievable stents for vasospasm
recommendations.text: Evidence is insufficient to support mechanical vasodilation by temporary retrievable-stent deployment for DCI-related deterioration with refractory severe vasospasm.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 5b; consensus 3

recommendations.text: Evidence does not establish that neuroimaging rather than regular neurological examination improves functional outcome in adult aSAH; no recommendation can be made.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 6a; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: For clinical deterioration after aSAH, obtain plain head CT together with CT perfusion to identify the cause.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 6a; consensus 1

recommendations.section: PICO 6a: Imaging when examination is unavailable
recommendations.text: If neurological assessment is not possible and DCI risk is high, obtain plain head CT and CT perfusion at least once between days 4 and 14.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 6a; consensus 2

recommendations.text: Do not routinely use digital subtraction angiography to screen for macrovascular vasospasm after aSAH.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 6a; consensus 3

recommendations.text: No evidence-based recommendation can be made for neuromonitoring rather than regular neurological examination to improve functional outcome in adult aSAH.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 6b; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: The panel could not give a recommendation for or against TCD monitoring in aSAH.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 6b; consensus 1

recommendations.text: If a patient with aSAH and radiological hydrocephalus cannot be assessed neurologically, monitor ICP through the EVD when an EVD is already in place.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 6b; consensus 2

recommendations.text: For neurologically unassessable aSAH without radiological hydrocephalus, the panel could not recommend whether to monitor ICP.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 6b; consensus 3

recommendations.text: In neurologically unassessable aSAH, avoid invasive multimodal monitoring using continuous brain tissue oxygen tension and/or microdialysis because the risk–benefit balance is uncertain.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 6b; consensus 4

recommendations.text: Do not routinely use continuous EEG monitoring in aSAH patients who cannot be assessed neurologically.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 6b; consensus 5

recommendations.text: No evidence-based recommendation can be made on CSF diversion strategies to improve functional outcome in aSAH with hydrocephalus.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 7; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Use CSF drainage for aSAH with radiological hydrocephalus and decreased consciousness. Consensus 13/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 7; consensus 1

recommendations.text: Place an EVD for aSAH with obstructive hydrocephalus and decreased consciousness. Consensus 13/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 7; consensus 2

recommendations.text: For communicating hydrocephalus with decreased consciousness, favour lumbar drainage or repeated lumbar punctures as the initial CSF-diversion approach. Consensus 11/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 7; consensus 3

recommendations.text: Do not drain CSF solely for radiological hydrocephalus when consciousness is normal. Consensus 12/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 7; consensus 4

recommendations.text: Use permanent CSF diversion when the serious-complication risk of prolonged EVD, lumbar drainage or repeated lumbar puncture exceeds that of a permanent diversion procedure. Consensus 13/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 7; consensus 5

recommendations.text: Use permanent CSF diversion for symptomatic chronic hydrocephalus after aSAH. Consensus 13/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 7; consensus 6

recommendations.text: Evidence does not establish a recommendation for neuro-ICU or high-care admission specifically to improve functional outcome after aSAH.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 8; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Admit and manage aSAH patients in a dedicated neuro-ICU or high-care unit. Consensus 13/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 8; consensus 1

recommendations.text: No evidence-based recommendation can be made for high-volume-centre admission or transfer to improve functional outcome after aSAH.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 9a; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Admit or immediately transfer spontaneous SAH patients to centres treating ≥70 aSAH patients per year; in remote areas with limited access, the threshold is ≥35 per year. Consensus 12/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 9a; consensus 1

recommendations.section: PICO 9b: Operator annual case volume evidence
recommendations.text: No evidence-based recommendation can be made on neurosurgeon or neurointerventionalist case volume to improve functional outcome after aSAH.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 9b; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Aneurysm repair should be performed by a neurosurgeon or neurointerventionalist who uses the chosen treatment in >30 aneurysm patients, ruptured and unruptured, annually. Consensus 12/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 9b; consensus 1

recommendations.text: No evidence-based recommendation can be made for radiological follow-up beyond 6 months after clipping or endovascular treatment specifically to improve functional outcome.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 10; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: After coiling with adequate occlusion confirmed within 6 months, obtain at least one additional imaging follow-up at or beyond 12 months after repair to assess recanalisation while retreatment remains an option. Consensus 13/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 10; consensus 1

recommendations.text: After microsurgical clipping with adequate occlusion confirmed within 6 months, further imaging for recanalisation is not suggested. Consensus 11/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 10; consensus 2

recommendations.section: PICO 10: Residual or partially occluded aneurysm
recommendations.text: For neck remnants or partial occlusion after any repair technique, continue imaging beyond 6 months while retreatment remains possible. Consensus 13/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 10; consensus 3

recommendations.section: PICO 10: Endovascular devices other than coils
recommendations.text: After treatment with endovascular devices other than coils, obtain imaging follow-up at least 5 years after treatment, regardless of initial occlusion, to check long-term occlusion while retreatment remains an option. Consensus 11/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 10; consensus 4

recommendations.text: For a high-risk profile, such as young age, familial aSAH or autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, continue imaging beyond 6 months at 5-year intervals to detect de novo aneurysms while treatment remains an option. Consensus 12/13.
recommendations.sourceReference: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7); PICO 10; consensus 5

coverage.scope: All formal recommendations and good-practice/consensus statements
coverage.sourceTable: Individual PICO boxes aakag043fx3.jpg through aakag043fx32.jpg; Table 3 images aakag043fx33-1.jpg through aakag043fx33-5.jpg (online table stops within PICO 7)
coverage.countingNote: 15 PICO questions; PICO 4 contains three separately graded statements, giving 17 formal/no-recommendation entries. All 37 separately numbered or standalone consensus statements are individual entries.
